name: MonarchInlineCodeStyle
title: InlineCode
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.ui.text.SpanStyle in an androidx.compose.ui.text.AnnotatedString, drawn by androidx.compose.material3.Text
summary: The look of a code fragment inside running text, as a SpanStyle of an AnnotatedString: the code typeface at 0.9 of the surrounding size, on the muted background (Subtle) or without one (Plain).
whenToUse: For a function name, a path, a command or a value to type inside a sentence. Use markdown for text with backticks, annotatedString for a single fragment, spanStyle with buildAnnotatedString for anything else.
whenNotToUse: For a block of code on its own lines use MonarchText in the Code role. For a keyboard shortcut use MonarchKbd.
api: fun spanStyle(colors: MonarchColors, typography: MonarchTypography, variant: MonarchInlineCodeVariant = MonarchInlineCodeVariant.Subtle): SpanStyle
@Composable @ReadOnlyComposable fun annotatedString(code: String, variant: MonarchInlineCodeVariant = MonarchInlineCodeVariant.Subtle): AnnotatedString
@Composable @ReadOnlyComposable fun markdown(text: String, variant: MonarchInlineCodeVariant = MonarchInlineCodeVariant.Subtle): AnnotatedString

options.name: variant
options.description: Subtle draws the muted background behind the code and uses the default text color; Plain only switches to the code typeface and keeps the surrounding color.

options.name: text
options.description: In markdown, the text with backticks around the code.

options.name: colors, typography
options.description: In the non-composable spanStyle, the theme to take the roles from, for code outside composition.

appearance: Subtle: the code typeface in the default text color on the muted background. Plain: the code typeface in the color of the surrounding text. Both follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes when built inside composition.
platformNotes: The web InlineCode is an element; in Compose running text is one Text, so Monarch provides a span style and helpers that build AnnotatedString runs, as iOS builds AttributedString runs. Text draws the background flush with the characters: the padding and rounded corners of the web chip are not available. The code is 0.9em of the surrounding text, as on the web (iOS uses the full size). The web nowrap option is not offered; a long token breaks where it does not fit. The parity map named MonarchTypography; it has a Code role for whole texts but nothing for a run inside a sentence, so the style is shipped under the iOS name MonarchInlineCodeStyle.
accessibility: The code run is part of the text and TalkBack reads it in place, as its characters.
Code differs from the text around it by the monospaced face, so it is recognisable without the background color, also in the Plain variant.
The size is relative (0.9em), so the code grows with the surrounding text and the font size setting.
edgeCases: A SpanStyle holds resolved colors. Build it in composition from the theme so that it follows light, dark and high contrast; the non-composable spanStyle takes the theme's colors explicitly.
markdown reads backticks only. An unmatched backtick and the text after it are shown unchanged; an empty pair of backticks is removed.
Ligatures are turned off in the code run, so -> and != are shown as typed.
A long token such as a hash wraps where it does not fit a line.
